alerts.detail:
There is a logging cable and pulley spanning across the river. It has not been used in years. It has generally been high enough not to be an issue. Something happened and the cable is sagging close to the water.
The rapids is runnable to the left with enough clearance. The rapids should not be run on the right. The pulley mechanism is less than 2’ from the water surface when the river was running 7’ yesterday.

-Chester Cohen

I have very sad news to share, a gentleman we paddled with today (we only knew him as Bill) lost his life on the Iron Bridge rapid this afternoon. Two young kayakers pulled him from the hole and performed CPR for almost 20 minutes until help finally arrived. It was truly a heroic effort, unfortunately in vain.

Please say a prayer for Bill and his family.
\-\-\-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
10-18-11
Official cause of death has been listed as a cervical fracture. AW Public Accident report has been uploaded.

detail.description:
## **[Video Guide Click Here](https://youtu.be/rgldw4nfiJ0)**

**Logistics:**

See the [Lower Moose Map](http://www.americanwhitewater.org/photos/?photoid=13873). The normal putin is at Rock Island, off Moose River Road, about three miles West of Rte. 28. The takeout is at Fowlerville Road, the normal putin for the Bottom Moose. To get to the takeout from the putin, continue West on Moose River Road for about 4 miles.

Bear Right at Porter's Corners, staying on Moose River Road.

After another 2.5 miles, take a Right onto North South Road.

At the T intersection, hang Left onto Penny Settlement Road.

After a short drive, take your first Right onto Fowlerville Road. The river's about a mile and a half along Fowlerville. Park before the river, on the left or the right. (There's a good sandy parking area on the left.)

See also the [Google Directions from Utica.](http://maps.google.com/maps?f=q&hl=en&q=Utica,+NY+to+43.6086006N,+75.161499W&ie=UTF8&z=9&ll=43.355141,-75.171204&spn=0.858741,1.966553&om=1)

Those wishing to run the class-4 section usually put in at Rock Island. Those wishing to run the class-3 section (Middle Moose) usually take out at Rock Island: Longitude - 75, 09, 27 and Latitude 43, 36, 01.

See also the [Middle Moose](http://www.americanwhitewater.org/content/River_detail_id_3590_), Class III, and [Bottom Moose](http://www.americanwhitewater.org/content/River_detail_id_1352_), Class V.

High Runnable (R6-R9): 6 - 10 cfs  Comment: This gets really big above 6 feet; you probably need to sneak some stuff in this range. When in doubt, scoudt!
Low Runnable (R0-R4): 3.8 - 4.2 cfs  Comment: It gets quite bony much below 4 ft, but the rapids can still be real at the lower levels.
Medium Runnable (R4-R6): 4.21 - 6 cfs  Comment: This is a rough approximation of the medium level. We know that it gets significantly pushier somewhere between 4 and 5 feet.
